title: Vasquez still allows saying images are adored with latria—per accidents, via exterior signs
source_text: LX. Caeterum tamen pertendit, absolute dici posse imagines adorari adoratione latriae. Quanquam enim imaginibus non sit deferendus ille servitutis affectus, qui latria dicitur, per accidens tamen latria coluntur: idque quoniam imaginibus defertur exterior adoratio, per signa derivata ab affectu servitutis latriae circa exemplar; quod satis esse putat, ut dicatur imago per accidens cum prototypo, non per se, adoratione latriae adorari.
pass_a_gloss: Yet nevertheless he maintains that it can absolutely be said that images are adored with the adoration of latria. For although that affect of servitude which is called latria is not to be deferred to images, yet they are cultivated with latria per accidents: and that because exterior adoration is deferred to images, through signs derived from the affect of latria-servitude about the exemplar; which he thinks is enough for it to be said that the image is adored with the adoration of latria per accidents with the prototype, not per se.
pass_b_english: Vasquez still allows absolute speech that images are adored with latria—but only per accidents.
Exterior signs drawn from latria-servitude toward the exemplar make the image latria-adored with the prototype, not per se.

lemmas.gloss: yet they are cultivated with latria by accident

choices.why: Exterior marks flowing from latria-affect toward the exemplar.
